subject: extract \hat\sigma values for each mean in “regions.xls”

messages.author: 4cfe772c0ef05101
messages.subject: extract \hat\sigma values for each mean in “regions.xls”
parts:
Hi People,

I have the following sequence of commands:

chipType <- "GenomeWideSNP_5";
cdfTags <- "Full,r2";
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, tags=cdfTags)
print(cdf)
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf)
print(gi)
si <- getSnpInformation(cdf)
print(si)
acs <- AromaCellSequenceFile$byChipType(getChipType(cdf, fullname=FALSE))
print(acs)
csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("sleData", cdf=cdf)
print(csR)
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(csR, model="CRMAv2")
print(acc)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
print(csC)
bpn <- BasePositionNormalization(csC, target="zero")
print(bpn)
csN <- process(bpn, verbose=verbose)
print(csN)
plm <- AvgCnPlm(csN, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300)
print(plm)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
print(ces)
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces, target="zero")
print(fln)
cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)
print(cesN)
ceR <- getAverageFile(cesN, verbose=verbose)
print(ceR)
cbs <- CbsModel(cesN)
print(cbs)
chrs<-seq(1,22)
fit(cbs,chromosomes=chrs,verbose=verbose)
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cbs)
print(ce)
process(ce, chromosomes=chrs, verbose=verbose)


The last command creates a number of graphic files, each of which
displays the estimate of standard errors (\hat\sigma_{\delta}). Is
there any way to get these estimates as a sequence of numbers
corresponding to each “mean” in the “regions.xls”?

Thanks

Max

>

> The last command creates a number of graphic files, each of which
> displays the estimate of standard errors (\hat\sigma_{\delta}). Is
> there any way to get these estimates as a sequence of numbers
> corresponding to each “mean” in the “regions.xls”?

That standard deviation is estimated via a robust first-order
difference variance estimator, where *\Delta* in the index indicates a
"difference". If (C_1,C_2,...,C_T) are the ordered copy numbers along
the genome, then this variance estimator for *the whole genome* is:

V[C] = mad(D) / sqrt(2)

where the first-order differences are D_{t} = C_{t+1} - C_{t}. By
calculating it this way, the variance estimate is robust against
change points, that is, we don't have to know the change point when
using it.

To estimate the standard deviation for a particular array and
chromosome this way, do:

rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=3, chromosome=9);
sigma <- estimateStandardDeviation(rawCNs);

plot(rawCNs);
text <- substitute(hat(sigma)[Delta]==sd, list(sd=sprintf("%.3g", sigma)));
stext(text=text, side=3, pos=0.5, line=-2);

To estimate the same for a specific region, you can extract the region
first and then repeat, e.g.

rawCNsB <- extractRegion(rawCNs, region=c(24.2, 28.5)*1e6);
sigmaB <- estimateStandardDeviation(rawCNsB);

Hope this helps

/Henrik

>
> Thanks
>
> Max

messages.subject: Re: extract \hat\sigma values for each mean in “regions.xls”
parts:
Thanks for your information Henrik.

1. I can extract sigma estimates using you first suggestion:

rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=3, chromosome=9);
sigma <- estimateStandardDeviation(rawCNs);

A colleague of mine recommended an alternative way apparently leading
to the same results (in slightly different form):

sigmas_all_arrays <- estimateSds(cbs, chromosomes=seq(1,22))

So, this questions is addressed.

2. It would be good to obtain sigmas for each region given in
“regions.xls” and you suggest it can be implemented as:

rawCNsB <- extractRegion(rawCNs, region=c(24.2, 28.5)*1e6);
sigmaB <- estimateStandardDeviation(rawCNsB);

However, there is immediately an error message:

Error: could not find function "extractRegion"

Could you clarify why and how to obtain these region specific sigmas.

Thank you.

Max

So, I forgot about that method - it is basically a wrapper of the
above looping of arrays and chromosomes requested. FYI, there is a
reason why many of these methods are not documented online - it's that
these are not part of a public and stable API. As I find methods to
settled over time I reveal them one by one (or when people really beg
for them).

>

> 2. It would be good to obtain sigmas for each region given in

> sigmaB <- estimateStandardDeviation(rawCNsB);

> However, there is immediately an error message:
>
> Error: could not find function "extractRegion"

The 'rawCNs' object is the one you extract above using
extractRawCopyNumbers(), e.g.
> rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=3, chromosome=9);

> print(rawCNs)
RawCopyNumbers:
Name:
Chromosome: 9
Position range: [239391,1.36968e+08]
Number of loci: 487
Mean distance between loci: 281336
Loci fields: x [487xnumeric], y [487xnumeric]
RAM: 0.01MB

In order to retrieve the regions of interest from the 'regions.xls'
file, I suggest that you use the read.table() function. However, it
probably makes more sense to just grab the regions by calling fit() on
the CbsModel (again). This won't take much longer, because the
segmentation results are stored to file so when you call it a second,
it will be retrieved from file (instead of running CBS), e.g.

aa <- 3;
chr <- 19;

# Segment
fit <- fit(cbs, array=aa, chromosome=chr, .retResults=TRUE);
fit <- fit[[1]][[chr]];

# Get data frame of regions for this array and chromosome (same as in
regions.xls)
regions <- getRegions(fit);
print(regions);

if (nrow(regions) > 0) {
# Add a sigma column
regions$sigma <- as.double(NA);

# Extract full-resolution (raw) CNs
allCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=aa, chromosome=chr);

for (rr in seq(length=nrow(regions))) {
region <- c(regions$start[rr], regions$stop[rr]);
regCNs <- extractRegion(allCNs, region=region);
sigma <- estimateStandardDeviation(regCNs);
regions$sigma[rr] <- sigma;
} # for (rr ...)
} # if (...)
print(regions);

/Henrik

>
> Could you clarify why and how to obtain these region specific sigmas.
>
> Thank you.
>
> Max
